systems.name: Apache Tika
systems.description: Broad content detection and text/metadata extraction across heterogeneous document and binary formats.

systems.name: Soufflé
systems.description: Datalog system specialized for high-performance recursive relational and static-analysis workloads.

systems.name: Roslyn
systems.description: Compiler APIs exposing C# and Visual Basic syntax, symbols, binding, semantic models, diagnostics, and code transformations.

systems.name: Tree-sitter
systems.description: Incremental, error-tolerant concrete syntax parsing designed for source files that may be incomplete or changing.

systems.name: CUE
systems.description: Constraint/unification language that combines configuration values, schemas, defaults, validation, and composition.

systems.name: Pandoc
systems.description: Structured document conversion engine spanning many markup, publishing, and document formats.

systems.name: Apache Lucene
systems.description: Embedded full-text search/indexing library with mature analyzers, ranking, faceting, query machinery, and vector search.

systems.name: FFmpeg
systems.description: Media probing, demuxing, transcoding, filtering, streaming, and codec orchestration across a very broad format surface.

licensing.notes: Deployment obligations depend on enabled components and build configuration.

systems.name: GDAL
systems.description: Geospatial raster/vector format access, coordinate transformation, reprojection, and conversion infrastructure.

systems.name: jq
systems.description: Compact functional query and transformation language specialized for JSON streams and structured pipeline surgery.

systems.name: OPA / Rego
systems.description: Policy-as-code engine for evaluating shared declarative policy over arbitrary structured input.

systems.name: Racket / Redex
systems.description: Executable operational-semantics framework for defining, reducing, testing, and exploring programming-language models.

systems.name: Z3
systems.description: General SMT solver covering combinations of Boolean, arithmetic, bit-vector, array, datatype, and uninterpreted-function theories.

systems.name: cvc5
systems.description: General SMT theorem prover with broad theory support and value as an independent solver/reference implementation.

systems.name: MiniZinc
systems.description: Solver-independent high-level constraint modeling language for scheduling, allocation, finite-domain, and optimization problems.

systems.name: clingo
systems.description: Grounder and solver for answer-set programming, suited to combinatorial world construction with defaults and exceptions.

systems.name: SWI-Prolog
systems.description: Mature Prolog system with constraint libraries for goal-directed relational search and partially instantiated terms.

systems.name: TLA+ / PlusCal / TLC
systems.description: Specification and model-checking ecosystem for concurrent and distributed state-transition systems.

systems.name: Alloy
systems.description: Relational modeling language and bounded model finder for structural invariants, graphs, ownership, cardinality, and counterexamples.

systems.name: Dafny
systems.description: Verification-aware programming language with contracts, invariants, automated proofs, and compilation to mainstream target languages.

systems.name: Lean 4
systems.description: Interactive theorem prover and functional language for machine-checked mathematics and software proofs.

systems.name: Julia / SciML / Symbolics
systems.description: Composable numerical and symbolic ecosystem where generic mathematical types can flow through solvers, AD, optimization, and generated numerical code.

systems.name: Wolfram Engine
systems.description: Broad exact and symbolic computation engine suitable as an independently implemented mathematical oracle.

licensing.notes: Free Engine has development/pre-production restrictions; production classification requires license review.

systems.name: Nix
systems.description: Reproducible package/build/environment system that models dependency closures explicitly.

systems.name: Lua
systems.description: Small embeddable scripting language with a deliberately simple host API and low runtime footprint.

systems.name: Verilator
systems.description: Compiles synthesizable Verilog/SystemVerilog into fast native C++/SystemC models for executable simulation and software-style testing.

triggers.smell: I am accumulating one parser per incoming file type.
triggers.description: Unknown or mixed document/binary formats must be normalized into text and metadata.
positive_signals: format coverage matters more than pixel-perfect layout
negative_signals: only one known format
exact visual layout reconstruction is the primary requirement

triggers.smell: I have a work queue that propagates facts until nothing changes.
triggers.description: The core computation is monotone recursive relational propagation or transitive closure.
negative_signals: side effects and ordering dominate
the workload is primarily numerical

triggers.smell: I need to know what C# code means, not merely how it parses.
triggers.description: Analysis requires binding, overload resolution, symbols, inferred types, diagnostics, or compiler-faithful refactoring.
negative_signals: only concrete syntax structure is needed
the language is not C# or Visual Basic

triggers.smell: I need syntax trees while source is incomplete, malformed, or changing interactively.
triggers.description: The core need is incremental and error-tolerant concrete syntax across one or more programming languages.
negative_signals: compiler-faithful semantic binding is required

triggers.smell: Configuration is turning into schema + defaults + overlays + custom validation code.
triggers.description: Configuration composition and validation are becoming a constraint system in disguise.
negative_signals: configuration is flat and static
a conventional schema already expresses every required rule cleanly

triggers.smell: I am writing pairwise converters among documentation and publishing formats.
triggers.description: The need is structured conversion among markup, office, publishing, or ebook formats rather than extraction from arbitrary binaries.
negative_signals: the primary need is arbitrary binary content extraction
pixel-identical rendering is required

triggers.smell: I am building a serious local search engine inside an application.
triggers.description: The application needs embedded indexing, analyzers, ranking, faceting, rich queries, or vector search without operating a separate search server.
negative_signals: simple exact lookup is sufficient
an external search service is already operationally preferred

triggers.smell: I am starting to write codec/container/transcoding glue.
triggers.description: The workload requires probing, converting, filtering, muxing, streaming, or combining diverse audio/video formats.
negative_signals: only one trivial codec path is needed
a platform-native API already completely owns the requirement

triggers.smell: I am writing geospatial format and coordinate-system plumbing.
triggers.description: Raster/vector ingestion, reprojection, coordinate transforms, or conversion across geospatial formats dominates the task.
negative_signals: the data has no geospatial coordinate semantics

triggers.smell: I need a small program just to reshape JSON in a pipeline.
triggers.description: The task is primarily selection, projection, filtering, grouping, or transformation of JSON streams.
negative_signals: the transformation needs substantial application state or domain logic

triggers.smell: The same policy logic is being reimplemented at several enforcement points.
triggers.description: Heterogeneous systems need a shared declarative decision engine over structured input.
negative_signals: the rule is local and trivial
policy is inseparable from one application's domain workflow

triggers.smell: I am writing a programming-language semantics on paper and a separate interpreter to test it.
triggers.description: The artifact is an operational semantics, calculus, reduction system, or language model that should itself be executable and testable.
negative_signals: the goal is ordinary parsing or production compiler construction

triggers.smell: I am hand-writing search over arithmetic, bit-vectors, arrays, or logical constraints.
triggers.description: The core problem maps to SMT theories rather than custom enumeration.
negative_signals: domain structure is better expressed as CP scheduling or nonmonotonic rules

triggers.smell: I want to model scheduling/allocation constraints without committing to one solver API.
triggers.description: The problem is naturally a high-level constraint-programming or optimization model and solver interchangeability matters.
negative_signals: low-level SMT theories are the natural representation
solver-specific features dominate

triggers.smell: I am generating candidate worlds under defaults, exclusions, and combinatorial rules.
triggers.description: The problem is nonmonotonic combinatorial knowledge representation with admissible-model search.
negative_signals: the problem is straightforward monotone relational closure
numeric optimization dominates

triggers.smell: I keep writing recursive search where arguments may be known in either direction.
triggers.description: The computation is goal-directed relational search over partially instantiated terms, optionally with finite-domain constraints.
negative_signals: the workload is a large monotone whole-program fixed point
deterministic imperative flow is simpler

triggers.smell: The bug I fear is some legal interleaving of retries, messages, failover, or concurrent steps.
triggers.description: Correctness depends on state transitions and behaviors across nondeterministic concurrent or distributed executions.
negative_signals: the concern is purely structural rather than behavioral
the implementation/spec correspondence cannot be meaningfully modeled

triggers.smell: I want a tiny concrete counterexample to a structural invariant.
triggers.description: The model is primarily finite sets, relations, graphs, ownership, and cardinality constraints.
negative_signals: unbounded proof is required
behavioral traces and temporal properties dominate

triggers.smell: The proof obligation belongs directly beside executable implementation code.
triggers.description: Critical code needs contracts, loop invariants, representation invariants, and automated deductive verification.
negative_signals: the problem is better modeled separately as a protocol
interactive theorem proving is required

triggers.smell: Testing or bounded search is insufficient; I need a machine-checked proof.
triggers.description: A mathematical or program proposition must be discharged by an interactive prover and trusted kernel.
negative_signals: bounded model finding or SMT automation fully answers the real question
formalization cost outweighs the required assurance

triggers.smell: My custom mathematical objects keep falling out of the numerical stack.
triggers.description: Unusual scalar/types must compose through solvers, automatic differentiation, optimization, symbolic transforms, or generated code.
negative_signals: the job is ordinary tabular analysis or standard dense linear algebra

triggers.smell: I need an independently implemented exact/symbolic mathematical oracle.
triggers.description: The task needs broad symbolic manipulation, exact computation, equation solving, transforms, or differential-test reference answers.
negative_signals: ordinary floating-point numerics are sufficient
production licensing cost dominates the value

triggers.smell: Environment and toolchain drift has become part of the bug surface.
triggers.description: The project needs explicit, reproducible dependency/toolchain closures rather than best-effort environment setup.
negative_signals: a conventional lockfile/container already gives adequate reproducibility
team learning cost exceeds the drift problem

triggers.smell: My application needs a user/plugin scripting language and I am about to invent one.
triggers.description: A host application needs a small embeddable extension language with straightforward native bindings.
negative_signals: users require the full Python/JavaScript ecosystem
no runtime scripting is actually needed

triggers.smell: I want software-style fast tests or fuzzing over Verilog/SystemVerilog RTL.
triggers.description: RTL needs to become a fast native executable model for CI, differential testing, or large simulation workloads.
negative_signals: analog/mixed-signal behavior dominates
the required constructs are outside Verilator's supported simulation model

evidence.title: Crossing-Cost Advantage Atlas: Where Specialist Ecosystems Actually Earn the Boundary

recommendations.advantage: Deletes a large parser-integration subsystem by presenting broad document detection, text extraction, and metadata normalization behind one surface.
avoid_when: The corpus is one narrow well-supported format.
Exact page geometry or rendering fidelity is the actual product requirement.

closest_alternatives.name: format-specific host-language libraries
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer them when format scope is narrow and fidelity requirements are specific.

boundary.interface: Tika app/server or a tiny JBang/JVM wrapper
boundary.notes: Borrow the capability without making the whole application a Java application.

recommendations.example: Normalize a corpus containing PDFs, Office files, email containers, EPUB, archives, and metadata-heavy binaries into searchable text/metadata.

recommendations.advantage: Turns recursive fixed-point propagation into declarative Datalog and supplies optimized evaluation/indexing machinery instead of hand-maintained worklists.
avoid_when: Execution order and side effects are central to correctness.
The workload is dominated by numerical kernels rather than relations.

closest_alternatives.name: imperative worklist algorithm
closest_alternatives.reason: Keep it when the relation set is tiny or operational ordering itself is the point.

closest_alternatives.name: general database recursive CTEs
closest_alternatives.reason: Useful when the analysis already naturally lives inside an RDBMS and performance/expressiveness is sufficient.

boundary.interface: facts in / relations out, or compile to a generated executable

recommendations.example: Express whole-program reachability or taint propagation as recursive relations instead of queues, visited sets, and convergence loops.

recommendations.advantage: Uses the compiler's own semantic model for binding, symbols, overload resolution, diagnostics, and transformations instead of approximating C# meaning.
avoid_when: Only concrete syntax is needed.
The target language is outside Roslyn's compiler surface.

closest_alternatives.name: Tree-sitter
closest_alternatives.reason: Excellent for syntax, but deliberately does not provide C# compiler semantics.

boundary.interface: small .NET worker or direct library when the host is already .NET

recommendations.example: Refactor symbol usages correctly across aliases, generics, overloads, inferred types, and partial classes.

recommendations.advantage: Provides incremental, error-tolerant syntax trees across many languages and is designed for interactive source that may not currently compile.
avoid_when: Compiler-faithful symbol binding or type semantics are required.

closest_alternatives.name: Roslyn
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when actual C#/VB compiler semantics matter more than cross-language incremental syntax.

boundary.interface: native or Wasm binding

recommendations.example: Maintain syntax trees for a multi-language editor while users are halfway through typing invalid code.

recommendations.advantage: Collapses values, schemas, defaults, validation, and composition into one constraint/unification representation.
avoid_when: Configuration is flat, static, and already well-served by a conventional schema.
Introducing a new DSL costs more than the duplicated validation logic.

closest_alternatives.name: JSON Schema + templating/overlay system
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when validation is the only nontrivial concern and composition semantics remain simple.

boundary.interface: cue vet/export at build or configuration-generation time

recommendations.example: Replace YAML overlays plus defaults plus schema validation plus bespoke cross-field checks with a single constrained configuration model.

recommendations.advantage: Normalizes many structured document dialects through a common document AST, avoiding a matrix of pairwise converters.
avoid_when: Required conversion fidelity is outside Pandoc's supported semantics.
The problem is extraction from arbitrary binary formats rather than structured conversion.

closest_alternatives.name: Apache Tika
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer for broad content extraction/metadata normalization rather than format-to-format publishing conversion.

boundary.interface: pandoc executable with files/stdin/stdout
boundary.notes: This is usually not a reason to adopt Haskell.

recommendations.example: Convert Markdown, reStructuredText, LaTeX, HTML, DOCX, or EPUB through one maintained conversion engine.

recommendations.advantage: Provides a mature embedded search engine without requiring a separate search service or rebuilding indexing/ranking/query infrastructure.
avoid_when: Search needs are limited to simple exact lookup or basic database FTS.
Operational requirements already favor a dedicated external search cluster.

closest_alternatives.name: SQLite/PostgreSQL FTS
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when search needs are modest and keeping the index inside the existing database is more valuable than Lucene's feature surface.

boundary.interface: JVM library or thin local service

recommendations.example: Add local faceted full-text and vector search over a corpus without operating Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.

recommendations.advantage: Deletes broad codec/container/filtering integration by concentrating decades of media interoperability behind a CLI/library surface.
avoid_when: A single platform-native media API completely owns the narrow requirement.
Licensing obligations of the selected FFmpeg build are incompatible with deployment.

closest_alternatives.name: platform media APIs
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer for narrow platform-specific capture/playback workflows where cross-format breadth is unnecessary.

boundary.interface: ffprobe/ffmpeg subprocess

recommendations.example: Probe, transcode, trim, resample, filter, and remux heterogeneous audio/video without integrating individual codecs.

recommendations.advantage: Owns a vast portion of geospatial format and coordinate-system plumbing that is expensive and error-prone to recreate.
avoid_when: The data has no geospatial coordinate semantics.
The task is a narrow operation fully supported by an existing host GIS API.

closest_alternatives.name: host-language GIS libraries
closest_alternatives.reason: Often wrap GDAL or are preferable when only a narrow high-level operation is required.

boundary.interface: gdal* CLI first; bindings when repeated in-process calls justify them

recommendations.example: Reproject and convert mixed raster/vector datasets across CRS and file formats without implementing geodesy/format adapters.

recommendations.advantage: The representation matches the problem directly and crossing cost is effectively zero in pipeline-oriented JSON work.
avoid_when: The transformation needs substantial application state, I/O orchestration, or domain behavior.
The team cannot accept a separate command-line dependency.

closest_alternatives.name: host-language JSON code
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when transformation is embedded in larger domain logic rather than a standalone structured-data step.

boundary.interface: stdin/stdout

recommendations.example: Select, reshape, group, and join JSON emitted by another command without creating a throwaway application.

recommendations.advantage: Centralizes declarative policy semantics across heterogeneous enforcement points instead of duplicating policy code per service.
avoid_when: The policy is tiny, local, and inseparable from one application's workflow.
An existing platform policy engine already owns all enforcement points.

closest_alternatives.name: application-native authorization code
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when the policy surface is local and no cross-system consistency problem exists.

boundary.interface: local OPA process/REST or embedded evaluator

recommendations.example: Apply the same admission/authorization policy to services written in several different implementation languages.

recommendations.advantage: Makes the formal operational semantics itself executable, testable, and generative rather than maintaining a paper model plus a separate interpreter.
avoid_when: The goal is production compiler implementation rather than semantic modeling.
Only parsing or AST manipulation is needed.

closest_alternatives.name: handwritten reference interpreter
closest_alternatives.reason: May be preferable when the semantics are already simple and the formal model is not itself a deliverable.

boundary.interface: standalone Racket/Redex model and test suite

recommendations.example: Define a reduction calculus, evaluation contexts, and metafunctions and generate/test terms directly from that semantics.

recommendations.advantage: Replaces custom logical search with mature SMT theory reasoning and propagation across mixed Boolean/arithmetic/bit-vector structures.
avoid_when: Constraint programming globals/scheduling are the natural abstraction.
The problem is primarily nonmonotonic defaults/exceptions.

closest_alternatives.name: cvc5
closest_alternatives.reason: Use as an independent oracle or where its theory/proof capabilities better fit the workload.

boundary.interface: SMT-LIB process or host API

recommendations.example: Solve bit-vector and array constraints for a protocol or symbolic execution subproblem instead of writing bespoke enumeration.

recommendations.advantage: Offers an independent modern SMT implementation with broad theory support, useful both as a primary solver and as a cross-checking oracle.
avoid_when: Z3 already satisfies the workload and independent validation has no value.
The problem maps more naturally to CP or ASP.

closest_alternatives.name: Z3
closest_alternatives.reason: Often the default SMT choice because of its ecosystem and broad adoption.

boundary.interface: SMT-LIB process

recommendations.example: Differentially check SMT-dependent tooling against a second solver rather than trusting one implementation.

recommendations.advantage: Separates a high-level constraint model from solver choice, avoiding solver-specific imperative search code.
avoid_when: Solver-specific APIs/features are the core requirement.
The problem maps directly to SMT theories with no benefit from CP globals.

closest_alternatives.name: direct OR-Tools/solver API
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when solver lock-in is acceptable and programmatic integration outweighs model portability.

boundary.interface: .mzn model plus CLI/API

recommendations.example: Model scheduling/resource allocation once and compare multiple back-end solvers without rewriting the model.

recommendations.advantage: Represents combinatorial admissible-world search with defaults and exceptions directly, replacing hand-coded candidate generation/backtracking.
avoid_when: The logic is monotone recursive closure better expressed as Datalog.
The task is primarily continuous/numeric optimization.

closest_alternatives.name: SWI-Prolog
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer for goal-directed relational queries where query direction and partially instantiated terms matter.

boundary.interface: facts/rules in, stable models out; API when incremental solving is needed

recommendations.example: Choose a consistent set of actions/configurations under defaults, exclusions, and global combinatorial rules.

recommendations.advantage: Turns recursive search and bidirectional relations into direct language semantics through unification, backtracking, and CLP libraries.
avoid_when: The computation is a large monotone fixed point better suited to Datalog.
The relation is trivial enough that adding a runtime outweighs the modeling benefit.

closest_alternatives.name: Soufflé
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer for large bottom-up recursive relational analyses rather than goal-directed queries.

boundary.interface: separate Prolog process/Pengine or subsystem module

recommendations.example: Solve a relational puzzle or structural search where any argument may be unknown and constraints should propagate both directions.

recommendations.advantage: Explores nondeterministic state-machine behaviors before implementation details hide the concurrency structure, producing concrete counterexample traces.
avoid_when: The main correctness question is static/structural rather than behavioral.
The model cannot be kept meaningfully aligned with the implementation.

closest_alternatives.name: Alloy
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer for bounded relational structure/counterexamples rather than temporal behaviors.

boundary.interface: .tla/.cfg model checked in CI

recommendations.example: Explore retries, duplicate messages, failover, and leader transitions across all bounded interleavings.

recommendations.advantage: Expresses finite relational structure compactly and searches for small concrete counterexamples to invariants.
avoid_when: Absence of a bounded counterexample must constitute an unbounded proof.
Temporal behavior rather than structure is the main concern.

closest_alternatives.name: TLA+
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer for transition-system behavior and temporal properties.

boundary.interface: Alloy model plus analyzer/model finder

recommendations.example: Find a minimal ownership/membership graph that violates an apparently plausible schema invariant.

recommendations.advantage: Keeps executable code and deductive contracts/invariants together, with automated verification and compilation to mainstream targets.
avoid_when: A separate behavioral model answers the real question more cheaply.
The proof requires deep interactive mathematics beyond Dafny's intended workflow.

closest_alternatives.name: Lean 4
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when interactive theorem proving and mathematical formalization dominate over executable verified code.

boundary.interface: verified critical module compiled/exported into the host system

recommendations.example: Implement a critical algorithm with pre/postconditions and loop invariants, then compile the verified component for use elsewhere.

recommendations.advantage: Provides a trusted-kernel machine-checked proof environment when tests, bounded search, and SMT are not sufficient evidence.
avoid_when: The assurance requirement does not justify formalization cost.
The property is better handled automatically by SMT/model checking.

closest_alternatives.name: Rocq / Isabelle
closest_alternatives.reason: Proof-assistant choice depends heavily on libraries, logic, automation, and existing formal assets; no universal winner was established.

boundary.interface: separate Lean proof project checked in CI

recommendations.example: Prove a mathematical property or algorithmic invariant that must survive independent kernel checking.

recommendations.advantage: Lets unusual mathematical representations participate generically across symbolic transforms, AD, solvers, optimization, and native specialization.
avoid_when: The task is routine dataframe/scientific analysis already well-served by Python/R.
Only standard numeric kernels are needed and mature host libraries already dominate.

closest_alternatives.name: Python SciPy/JAX ecosystem
closest_alternatives.reason: Often preferable for standard scientific/ML workloads; the crossing case strengthens when custom mathematical types must compose end-to-end.

boundary.interface: Julia numerical subsystem or worker process

recommendations.example: Propagate units, dual numbers, arbitrary precision, or symbolic values through an ODE solver and optimization pipeline.

recommendations.advantage: Supplies a very broad independently implemented CAS surface for exact/symbolic reference computation and differential testing.
avoid_when: Open-source symbolic tooling already covers the required mathematics.
Production licensing or authentication constraints outweigh the coverage advantage.

closest_alternatives.name: SymPy / Julia Symbolics
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when their supported symbolic domain is sufficient and open deployment matters more than Wolfram breadth.

boundary.interface: wolframscript/local Wolfram Engine

crossing_cost.notes: Production and organizational-use classification requires explicit licensing care.

recommendations.example: Generate exact reference answers for differential/property tests of a numerical implementation.

recommendations.advantage: Makes the dependency/toolchain closure explicit enough to reproduce complex environments rather than relying on ambient machine state.
avoid_when: A lockfile plus container already provides adequate reproducibility.
The organization cannot justify Nix's substantial conceptual learning cost.

closest_alternatives.name: containers + language lockfiles
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when they already solve the actual reproducibility failures without introducing Nix's model.

boundary.interface: nix develop/build wrapped around the existing project

recommendations.example: Pin compiler, native libraries, code generators, and tools into a reproducible development/build closure.

recommendations.advantage: Provides a purpose-built small embeddable language/runtime instead of inventing a bespoke extension DSL or embedding a much heavier general runtime.
avoid_when: Users specifically need the Python/JavaScript package ecosystem.
The application does not actually need runtime scripting.

closest_alternatives.name: Python/V8 embedding
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when ecosystem breadth and familiar user language outweigh embedding size and host-API simplicity.

boundary.interface: Lua VM embedded through C API/FFI

recommendations.example: Expose host functions and domain objects to user scripts without creating and maintaining a custom expression language.

recommendations.advantage: Turns RTL into fast native executable models, enabling ordinary software CI, fuzzing, and differential-test techniques over hardware designs.
avoid_when: Analog/mixed-signal behavior dominates.
Required simulation semantics rely on constructs outside Verilator's intended model.

closest_alternatives.name: event-driven HDL simulators
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when full language simulation fidelity is more important than native compiled throughput.

boundary.interface: generated C++/SystemC executable model

recommendations.example: Compile a SystemVerilog design into a native test target and subject it to property/fuzz/differential testing.

experiments.title: Hostile mixed-format document corpus
experiments.hypothesis: Tika materially increases successful extraction coverage while reducing format-specific integration code.
success_criteria: Higher format coverage on the same corpus

experiments.title: Recursive analysis bake-off
experiments.hypothesis: Soufflé reduces implementation complexity for monotone recursive analyses without unacceptable performance cost.

experiments.title: Constraint-oriented configuration bake-off
experiments.hypothesis: CUE can replace a multi-layer schema/default/overlay/validation stack with a simpler single representation.

experiments.title: Compositional numerics torture test
experiments.hypothesis: Julia/SciML materially reduces glue when unusual mathematical types must compose through AD, solving, and optimization.
success_criteria: Custom mathematical type survives end-to-end without bespoke extension layers
